issue.title: [Bug] HostBuffer.truncate failed during pin eviction on AMD ROCm (Windows) - comfy-aimdo 0.6.0 + comfy-kitchen 0.2.40, MiniMaxH3 dynamic VRAM
issue.body:
## TL;DR

Dynamic VRAM dies with `RuntimeError: HostBuffer.truncate failed` when the pinned-memory pool fills up. I instrumented the exact failure point. Two findings that may be useful:

1. Growing `MAX_PINNED_MEMORY` makes it worse, not better — a larger budget lets the hostbuf grow larger (8 GB -> 19 GB), and `truncate()` on the tail of that larger hostbuf fails sooner (6 surviving evictions -> 1).
2. The failure is always the same size (~125 MB) at the tail of the hostbuf, always `registered=True`, always a `Linear` module in subset `weights-fast`.

This is likely the same defect as #15591 (open, reported on comfy-kitchen 0.2.31 / NVIDIA). It is still present on 0.2.40 and on AMD ROCm.

## Environment

- ComfyUI: 0.43.0
- comfy-aimdo: 0.6.0
- comfy-kitchen: 0.2.40
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0 (cp313, local wheel)
- Python: 3.13.9 (embedded)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro build 26200
- GPU: AMD
...
- Driver: 32.0.32015.2008 (2026-09-28)
[ERROR] !!! Exception during processing !!! aimdo memory compile error
RuntimeError: HostBuffer.truncate failed
RuntimeError: aimdo memory compile error
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure  (hipErrorLaunchFailure)
Stack is identical to #15591. After the exception, `reset_cast_buffers` / `offload_stream.synchronize()` reports the HIP error and the process dies. On this machine the GPU sometimes drops to `ConfigManagerErrorCode=31` afterwards (twice today).
22:04:32 TRUNCATE_FAIL subset=weights-fast module=Linear pin_size=125.10MB
         err=RuntimeError('HostBuffer.truncate failed')
Survived 6 budget warnings over ~90 s before failing.
22:35:19 TRUNCATE_FAIL subset=weights-fast module=Linear pin_size=125.02MB
Failed on the first budget warning. Same task, same machine, minutes apart.
- Pinned at failure: 26,036.8 MB (99.7%) -> 31,274.6 MB (99.8%)
2. `hostbuf.truncate()` failure correlates with hostbuf size, not with the shortfall. Exp 1 had shortfalls between 4.0 and 92.3 MB and succeeded 6 times; Exp 2 failed with a 39.6 MB shortfall on a 19 GB hostbuf.
3. The reclaim target is always a ~125 MB tail block with `registered=True`, so `truncate()` must `cudaHostUnregister` before shrinking. `hostbuf_size - target_offset` matches `pin_size` exactly every time, so the offset arithmetic in `partially_unload_ram()` looks correct — the failure is inside the C call `lib.hostbuf_truncate()`.
4. The same task also succeeded twice on this machine with identical params, so it is not deterministic — but once the pool is saturated, failure appears inevitable within the prompt.
3. Was the fix for #15591 (reported against 0.2.31) shipped in a comfy-kitchen release? We are on 0.2.40 and still see the identical trace on ROCm.
`--disable-dynamic-vram` (legacy) is expected to bypass the pin pool entirely; I have not yet benchmarked it on this machine and will update.

### Feature Idea

Hi,

After updating to ComfyUI 0.39.1, I’m running into a new problem related to how model paths are scanned.

My setup:

ComfyUI version: 0.39.1
OS: Windows 11
Models stored on: OneDrive (some local, many cloud‑only)
extra_model_paths.yaml: points to OneDrive folders containing multiple model subdirectories

I keep all my models (checkpoints, LoRAs, VAE, etc.) on a OneDrive drive.
Not all of these models are synchronized locally; many are stored as cloud‑only files.
I’ve been using an extra_model_paths.yaml file for a long time to point ComfyUI to my OneDrive model folders.
In previous ComfyUI versions, this worked fine. ComfyUI would see the models that were available locally and didn’t try to pull down everything from OneDrive.

Since updating to 0.39.1, ComfyUI now appears to scan all folders listed in extra_model_paths.yaml much more aggressively, and this triggers
...
If I rename / disable extra_model_paths.yaml, ComfyUI runs fine and OneDrive stops trying to sync everything. The issue only appears when extra_model_paths.yaml is active and pointing to OneDrive-backed folders.
Could you consider adjusting the directory scanning logic so it doesn’t trigger OneDrive to download every cloud‑only file, or providing a configuration option to limit how aggressively ComfyUI scans those paths (e.g., lazy discovery, or optional scan modes for network / cloud drives)?

issue.title: SeedVR2: CUDA illegal memory access (MMU NACK) above a total video size on RTX 5090, reproducible, process can hang
issue.body:
Native SeedVR2 video upscaling (x2) crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` once the input video passes a certain total size. It depends on frames x resolution, not on VRAM in use: 193 frames at 704x1088 pass, 241 crash, and 289 at 352x544 pass. It reproduces every time, at the same point: about 1 s after the SeedVR2 model loads, at the start of the first sampling step. Smaller jobs in the same process, before and after, run fine.

It reproduces on Windows (portable build) and on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2, ComfyUI from git with the Linux PyTorch wheel). It happens on ComfyUI v0.43.0 and v0.44.0, with both an int8 and an fp8 checkpoint, and on two drivers. No launch flag fixes it. The only setting that makes it pass is `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, which points to a stream-ordering race (details below).

On Windows, after some crashes the Python process can't
